259	# Three real mismatches in the reverse site (amplicon offsets 40, 44, 48)
260	# plus an N in the forward site. Tolerance 1: the reverse primer has more
261	# real differences than allowed, so it is "mismatched". Because the reverse
262	# primer cannot bind anywhere, no product is possible whatever the N hides:
263	# the assay is "no product", NOT "not assessable" (fixed in version 3).
264	# The 3 mismatches are spaced 4 bases apart, cutting the reverse site into
265	# stretches of at most 4 bases, so the near-miss search (which needs an exact
266	# 5-base stretch) reports "none close". This shows that limit honestly.
267	# Version 4: the forward site has 0 mismatches + 1 N, which fits an allowance
268	# of 1 even if the N is a mismatch, so the forward primer now "binds".
269	def case_mismatched_beats_unknown():
270	    seq = amplicon()
271	    for offset in (40, 44, 48):
272	        seq = change_base(seq, offset)
273	    seq = mutate(seq, 3, "N")
274	    target = filler(10) + seq + filler(10)
275	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
276	    print_report("Case 10: reverse truly mismatched, N elsewhere", result)
277	    check(result["outcomes"]["reverse"] == "mismatched", "reverse is 'mismatched'")
278	    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "binds", "forward binds: 1 N fits an allowance of 1")
279	    check(result["assay"] == "no product", "assay is 'no product': the reverse primer cannot bind")
280	    check(result["near_misses"]["reverse"] is None,
281	          "near-miss not found: no exact 5-base stretch left (known limit)")
282	
283	
284	# =============================================================================
285	# SECTION 4: CASES SOLVABLE BY HAND: EDGE CASES (version 3)
286	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
287	# Situations the earlier cases did not cover.
288	# =============================================================================
289	
290	# -- Case 11: a primer pairs with itself -------------------------------------
291	# Put the forward primer's reverse complement where the reverse site would be.
292	# The forward primer now binds "+" at 10..26 AND "-" at 46..62, so it makes a
293	# 52 bp product on its own; the reverse primer binds nowhere.
294	def case_self_pairing():
295	    target = filler(10) + FAKE_FORWARD + INSERT + reverse_complement(FAKE_FORWARD) + filler(10)
296	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
297	    print_report("Case 11: forward primer pairs with itself", result)
298	    product = result["products"][0]
299	    check((product["left"]["primer"], product["right"]["primer"]) == ("forward", "forward"),
300	          "the product is forward x forward")
301	    check(product_lengths(result) == [52], "it is 52 bp")
302	    check(result["outcomes"]["reverse"] == "mismatched", "the reverse primer does not bind")
303	
304	
305	# -- Case 12: overlapping primer sites ---------------------------------------
306	# A second reverse primer whose site starts INSIDE the forward site:
307	# site = last 5 bases of the forward site + first 11 bases of the insert.
308	# Forward site 10..26, overlapping reverse site 21..37 -> product 10..37 = 27 bp.
309	OVERLAP_REVERSE = reverse_complement(FAKE_FORWARD[-5:] + INSERT[:11])
310	
311	
312	def case_overlapping_sites():
313	    target = filler(10) + FAKE_FORWARD + INSERT[:11] + filler(10)
314	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, OVERLAP_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
315	    print_report("Case 12: primer sites overlap by 5 bases", result)
316	    check(site_of(result, "reverse")["start"] == 21, "reverse site starts at 21, inside the forward site")
317	    check(product_lengths(result) == [27], "one 27 bp product")
318	
319	
320	# -- Case 13: mismatch allowance too high for the primer length --------------
321	# 16 bases // (3 + 1) pieces = 4 bases per piece, shorter than k = 5,
322	# so the search cannot guarantee it finds every site. It must stop with an error.
323	def case_allowance_too_high():
324	    print("\n--- Case 13: 3 mismatches allowed on a 16-base primer ---")
325	    try:
326	        run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, amplicon(), max_mismatches=3)
327	        check(False, "an error is raised")
328	    except ValueError as error:
329	        print(f"  error message: {error}")
330	        check(True, "an error is raised instead of a silently incomplete search")
331	
332	
333	# -- Case 14: palindromic primer binds both strands at the same spot ---------
334	# GCATGCATATGCATGC is its own reverse complement, so ONE place in the target
335	# is a "+" site and a "-" site at once (both 10..26). The two sites face each
336	# other, but the "product" would be only 16 bp (< 20 minimum): no product.
337	PALINDROME = "GCATGCATATGCATGC"
338	
339	
340	def case_palindrome():
341	    target = filler(10) + PALINDROME + filler(10)
342	    result = run_model(PALINDROME, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
343	    print_report("Case 14: palindromic primer", result)
344	    strands = sorted((s["strand"], s["start"]) for s in result["sites"] if s["primer"] == "forward")
345	    check(strands == [("+", 10), ("-", 10)], "same spot found on both strands")
346	    check(result["assay"] == "no product", "no product (16 bp is below the 20 bp minimum)")
347	
348	
349	# -- Case 15: degenerate base in the primer ----------------------------------
350	# Forward primer with Y (= C or T) at offset 8: GTTCAGAGYTACTGAC.
351	# Genome C or T at that spot -> 0 mismatches. Genome A -> 1 mismatch,
352	# 16 - 8 = 8 bases from the 3' end, reported as "primer Y, genome A".
353	DEGENERATE_FORWARD = mutate(FAKE_FORWARD, 8, "Y")
354	
355	
356	def case_degenerate_primer():
357	    for genome_base in ("C", "T"):
358	        target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 8, genome_base) + filler(10)
359	        result = run_model(DEGENERATE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
360	        print_report(f"Case 15: primer Y, genome {genome_base}", result)
361	        check(site_of(result, "forward")["mismatches"] == 0, f"Y matches genome {genome_base}")
362	
363	    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 8, "A") + filler(10)
364	    result = run_model(DEGENERATE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
365	    print_report("Case 15: primer Y, genome A", result)
366	    check(site_of(result, "forward")["changes"] ==
367	          [{"from_3prime": 8, "primer": "Y", "genome": "A", "severity": "mild"}],
368	          "Y does not match genome A: 8 from 3' end, primer Y, genome A, mild")
369	
370	
371	# -- Case 16: probe binds inside the product ---------------------------------
372	# Probe = the 20-base insert, which sits between the primer sites.
373	def case_probe_binds():
374	    target = filler(10) + amplicon() + filler(10)
375	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, probe=FAKE_PROBE, max_mismatches=0)
376	    print_report("Case 16: probe binds inside the product", result)
377	    check(result["products"][0]["probe"] == "binds", "probe binds inside the 52 bp product")
378	    check(result["assay"] == "product", "assay is 'product'")
379	
380	
381	# -- Case 17: primers bind but the probe does not ----------------------------
382	# Three real mismatches in the insert (amplicon offsets 18, 25, 31), tolerance 1.
383	# Both primers still bind and copy the DNA, but the probe cannot bind, so a
384	# qPCR machine would see no fluorescence: "no signal".
385	def case_probe_mismatched():
386	    seq = amplicon()
387	    for offset in (18, 25, 31):
388	        seq = change_base(seq, offset)
389	    target = filler(10) + seq + filler(10)
390	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, probe=FAKE_PROBE, max_mismatches=1)
391	    print_report("Case 17: probe has 3 mismatches", result)
392	    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "binds" and result["outcomes"]["reverse"] == "binds",
393	          "both primers bind")
394	    check(result["products"][0]["probe"] == "mismatched", "the probe does not bind")
395	    check(result["assay"] == "no signal", "assay is 'no signal'")
396	
397	
398	# -- Case 18: deletion inside a primer site ----------------------------------
399	# Delete 2 bases from the middle of the forward site (amplicon offsets 6-7).
400	# Without gaps this looks like many mismatches; the near-miss search should
401	# explain it as ONE event: a 2-base deletion. (2 is the longest deletion a
402	# 16-base primer can show: 16 - 2 = 14 = MIN_MATCHED_BASES.)
403	def case_deletion():
404	    seq = amplicon()
405	    target = filler(10) + seq[:6] + seq[8:] + filler(10)
406	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
407	    print_report("Case 18: 2-base deletion in the forward site", result)
408	    miss = result["near_misses"]["forward"]
409	    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "mismatched", "forward is 'mismatched'")
410	    check(miss["events"] == 1, "near-miss is 1 event, not many mismatches")
411	    check((miss["indel"]["kind"], miss["indel"]["length"]) == ("deletion", 2), "explained as a 2-base deletion")
412	
413	
414	# -- Case 18b: a 6-base deletion is too long for a 16-base primer -----------
415	# Delete 6 bases (offsets 5-10): only 10 primer bases would still match,
416	# fewer than MIN_MATCHED_BASES (14), so the model refuses to guess.
417	def case_deletion_too_long():
418	    seq = amplicon()
419	    target = filler(10) + seq[:5] + seq[11:] + filler(10)
420	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
421	    print_report("Case 18b: 6-base deletion in a 16-base primer site", result)
422	    check(result["near_misses"]["forward"] is None, "no near-miss: too few matching bases to be sure")
423	
424	
425	# -- Case 19: insertion inside a primer site ---------------------------------
426	# Insert TTT into the middle of the reverse site (after amplicon offset 43).
427	def case_insertion():
428	    seq = amplicon()
429	    target = filler(10) + seq[:44] + "TTT" + seq[44:] + filler(10)
430	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
431	    print_report("Case 19: 3-base insertion in the reverse site", result)
432	    miss = result["near_misses"]["reverse"]
433	    check(result["outcomes"]["reverse"] == "mismatched", "reverse is 'mismatched'")
434	    check(miss["events"] == 1, "near-miss is 1 event")
435	    check((miss["indel"]["kind"], miss["indel"]["length"]) == ("insertion", 3), "explained as a 3-base insertion")
436	
437	
438	# =============================================================================
439	# SECTION 5: CASES SOLVABLE BY HAND: VERSION 4 LOGIC FIXES
440	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
441	# Genome ambiguity codes, graded 3' risk, and binding through a small
442	# insertion/deletion in the primer's 5' half. (Case 7b above covers the
443	# "missing data cannot change the answer" fix.)
444	# =============================================================================
445	
446	# -- Case 20: ambiguity codes in the genome ----------------------------------
447	# The forward primer has C at offset 8 (8 bases from the 3' end).
448	#   genome Y (C or T): might match, might not      -> unknown
449	#   genome R (A or G): cannot match a C             -> certain mismatch
450	#   primer Y vs genome Y: every option is accepted  -> certain match
451	def case_genome_ambiguity():
452	    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 8, "Y") + filler(10)
453	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
454	    print_report("Case 20a: primer C, genome Y", result)
455	    check(site_of(result, "forward")["unknown_from_3prime"] == [8], "genome Y is unknown, not a mismatch")
456	    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "not assessable", "forward is 'not assessable'")
457	
458	    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 8, "R") + filler(10)
459	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
460	    print_report("Case 20b: primer C, genome R, tolerance 0", result)
461	    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "mismatched", "genome R is a certain mismatch: 'mismatched'")
462	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
463	    print_report("Case 20b: primer C, genome R, tolerance 1", result)
464	    check(site_of(result, "forward")["changes"] ==
465	          [{"from_3prime": 8, "primer": "C", "genome": "R", "severity": "severe"}],
466	          "reported as primer C, genome R, severe")
467	
468	    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 8, "Y") + filler(10)
469	    result = run_model(DEGENERATE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
470	    print_report("Case 20c: primer Y, genome Y", result)
471	    forward_site = site_of(result, "forward")
472	    check(forward_site["outcome"] == "binds" and forward_site["unknown_from_3prime"] == [],
473	          "primer Y fully accepts genome Y: a certain match")
474	
475	
476	# -- Case 21: graded 3' risk -------------------------------------------------
477	# a) Only the reverse site's 3'-terminal mismatch (amplicon offset 36 C -> T):
478	#    G-T is mild, so the product's 3' risk is LOW.
479	# b) The forward site's 3'-terminal base is N, tolerance 1: the site binds
480	#    even if the N is a mismatch, but the 3' end is uncertain: POSSIBLE.
481	def case_graded_risk():
482	    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 36, "T") + filler(10)
483	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
484	    print_report("Case 21a: one mild mismatch at the 3' end", result)
485	    check(result["products"][0]["three_prime_risk"] == "low", "product 3' risk is LOW")
486	
487	    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 15, "N") + filler(10)
488	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
489	    print_report("Case 21b: N at the forward primer's 3' end", result)
490	    check(site_of(result, "forward")["outcome"] == "binds", "forward binds even if the N is a mismatch")
491	    check(result["products"][0]["three_prime_risk"] == "possible", "product 3' risk is POSSIBLE")
492	
493	
494	# -- Case 22: 1-base deletion in the primer's 5' half ------------------------
495	# Delete amplicon offset 2 (a T, 14 bases from the 3' end; the T beside it
496	# makes 15 an equally good answer). The 3' half is intact, so with 1 mismatch
497	# allowed the forward primer still binds, counting the gap as 1 mismatch.
498	# The product loses 1 base: 51 bp. With 0 mismatches allowed it does not bind.
499	def case_small_deletion_5prime():
500	    seq = amplicon()
501	    target = filler(10) + seq[:2] + seq[3:] + filler(10)
502	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
503	    print_report("Case 22: 1-base deletion in the 5' half, tolerance 1", result)
504	    forward_site = site_of(result, "forward")
505	    check((forward_site["indel"]["kind"], forward_site["indel"]["length"]) == ("deletion", 1),
506	          "forward binds through a 1-base deletion")
507	    check(forward_site["indel"]["from_3prime"][0] > 8, "the deletion is in the 5' half")
508	    check(product_lengths(result) == [51], "product is 51 bp (one base shorter)")
509	
510	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
511	    print_report("Case 22: same, tolerance 0", result)
512	    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "mismatched", "with 0 allowed the gap is too much")
513	
514	
515	# -- Case 22b: 1-base deletion in the primer's 3' half -----------------------
516	# Delete amplicon offset 13 (a G, 3 bases from the 3' end). A gap that close
517	# to the 3' end is not allowed to bind; the near-miss search explains it.
518	def case_small_deletion_3prime():
519	    seq = amplicon()
520	    target = filler(10) + seq[:13] + seq[14:] + filler(10)
521	    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
522	    print_report("Case 22b: 1-base deletion in the 3' half", result)
523	    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "mismatched", "forward is 'mismatched'")
524	    check(result["near_misses"]["forward"]["indel"] ==
525	          {"kind": "deletion", "length": 1, "from_3prime": (3, 3)},
526	          "near-miss: 1-base deletion 3 bases from the 3' end")
527	
528	
529	# =============================================================================
530	# SECTION 6: CHECKING THE SEARCH ITSELF
531	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
532	# The k-mer search is fast because it skips most positions. These checks make
533	# sure it never skips a real site, and never invents near-misses.
534	# =============================================================================
535	
536	def brute_force_sites(primer, target, max_mismatches):
537	    """The slow way: compare the primer at EVERY position on both strands."""
538	    found = set()
539	    for strand, pattern in (("+", primer), ("-", reverse_complement(primer))):
540	        for start in range(-len(pattern) + 1, len(target)):
541	            mismatches, unknowns = compare_site(target, start, pattern)
542	            if len(mismatches) <= max_mismatches and len(pattern) - len(unknowns) >= MIN_KNOWN_BASES:
543	                found.add((strand, start))
544	    return found
545	
546	
547	def random_test_target(rng):
548	    """A 300-base random target with mutated primer copies, Ns/Ys and maybe a cut end."""
549	    target = [rng.choice("ACGT") for _ in range(300)]
550	    for _ in range(4):
551	        copy = list(FAKE_FORWARD if rng.random() < 0.5 else reverse_complement(FAKE_FORWARD))
552	        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
553	            copy[rng.randrange(len(copy))] = rng.choice("ACGT")
554	        position = rng.randrange(-6, 300 - len(copy) + 6)
555	        for i, base in enumerate(copy):
556	            if 0 <= position + i < len(target):
557	                target[position + i] = base
558	    for i in range(len(target)):
559	        if rng.random() < 0.02:
560	            target[i] = rng.choice("NY")
561	    return "".join(target)
562	
563	
564	# -- Case 23: fast search finds exactly what the slow search finds -----------
565	# 200 random targets x mismatch allowances 0, 1 and 2. Plain (ungapped) sites
566	# from the model must equal the slow every-position search exactly.
567	def case_search_complete():
568	    print("\n--- Case 23: fast search vs slow every-position search ---")
569	    rng = random.Random(23)
570	    compared = 0
571	    for _ in range(200):
572	        target = random_test_target(rng)
573	        for max_mismatches in (0, 1, 2):
574	            result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=max_mismatches)
575	            fast = {(s["strand"], s["start"]) for s in result["sites"]
576	                    if s["primer"] == "forward" and s["indel"] is None}
577	            slow = brute_force_sites(FAKE_FORWARD, target, max_mismatches)
578	            if fast != slow:
579	                raise AssertionError(f"fast {sorted(fast)} != slow {sorted(slow)} for {target}")
580	            compared += len(slow)
581	    check(True, f"600 searches agree with the slow search ({compared} sites compared)")
582	
583	
584	# -- Case 24: no invented near-misses on a random genome ---------------------
585	# A random 30,000-base sequence (the size of SARS-CoV-2) should not contain
586	# the CDC N1 primers or probe, and the near-miss search must not invent a
587	# "close" site there. (Before the MIN_MATCHED_BASES rule, it did.)
588	def case_random_genome():
589	    print("\n--- Case 24: CDC N1 primers on a random 30,000-base sequence ---")
590	    rng = random.Random(24)
591	    genome = "".join(rng.choice("ACGT") for _ in range(30000))
592	    result = run_model("GACCCCAAAATCAGCGAAAT", "TCTGGTTACTGCCAGTTGAATCTG", genome,
593	                       probe="ACCCCGCATTACGTTTGGTGGACC")
594	    check(result["sites"] == [], "no binding sites")
595	    check(all(miss is None for miss in result["near_misses"].values()), "no near-misses invented")
596	
597	
598	# =============================================================================
599	# SECTION 7: RUN EVERY CASE
600	# =============================================================================
601	
602	if __name__ == "__main__":
603	    case_exact_match()
604	    case_reverse_strand()
605	    case_mismatches()
606	    case_mismatch_5prime()
607	    case_multiple_products()
608	    case_facing_away()
609	    case_no_site()
610	    case_n_in_site()
611	    case_n_cannot_change_answer()
612	    case_truncated_end()
613	    case_truncated_start()
614	    case_mismatched_beats_unknown()
615	    case_self_pairing()
616	    case_overlapping_sites()
617	    case_allowance_too_high()
618	    case_palindrome()
619	    case_degenerate_primer()
620	    case_probe_binds()
621	    case_probe_mismatched()
622	    case_deletion()
623	    case_deletion_too_long()
624	    case_insertion()
625	    case_genome_ambiguity()
626	    case_graded_risk()
627	    case_small_deletion_5prime()
628	    case_small_deletion_3prime()
629	    case_search_complete()
630	    case_random_genome()
631	    print("\nAll cases passed.")

# =============================================================================
# TESTS FOR: FIRST MODEL: FACTOR: SPECIFICITY   (version 4)
# =============================================================================
# The model itself lives in first_model_factor_specificity.py; this file only
# tests it. Every case uses FAKE primers and a FAKE target built by hand, so
# each expected answer is worked out on paper first ("Cases solvable by hand"
# in the proposal). journal/test_cases_specificity.txt lists every case.
#
# Run it with:  python3 journal/test_first_model_factor_specificity.py
# =============================================================================

import random

from first_model_factor_specificity import (
    compare_site, print_report, reverse_complement, run_model, MIN_KNOWN_BASES,
)


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 1: FAKE PRIMERS AND FAKE TARGET BUILDING BLOCKS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fake target is assembled from pieces of known length, so every expected
# position and product size below can be added up by hand.
#
# Filler is poly-A: it cannot match any 5-base seed of these primers, so it
# never creates accidental binding sites.
# =============================================================================

FAKE_FORWARD = "GTTCAGAGCTACTGAC"   # 16 bases
FAKE_REVERSE = "TCCGATAGTCAGCTTG"   # 16 bases

# Where the reverse primer sits on the plus strand (as its reverse complement)
REVERSE_SITE = reverse_complement(FAKE_REVERSE)   # "CAAGCTGACTATCGGA"

INSERT = "CGTACGTTGCATGCCTAGGT"     # 20 bases between the two primer sites
FAKE_PROBE = INSERT                 # the probe binds the whole insert


def filler(n):
    """n bases of background sequence that no primer can bind."""
    return "A" * n


def amplicon():
    """forward site + insert + reverse site = 16 + 20 + 16 = 52 bp product."""
    return FAKE_FORWARD + INSERT + REVERSE_SITE


def mutate(seq, offset, new_base):
    """Return seq with the base at offset replaced (used to plant mismatches or Ns)."""
    return seq[:offset] + new_base + seq[offset + 1:]


def change_base(seq, offset):
    """Plant a guaranteed mismatch: A becomes C, anything else becomes A."""
    return mutate(seq, offset, "C" if seq[offset] == "A" else "A")


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 2: CASES SOLVABLE BY HAND: CORE (version 1)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each case states its expected answer (worked out on paper), runs the model,
# and checks the model agrees. A failed check stops the program.
# Positions in the checks are 0-based (as stored); the report prints 1-based.
# =============================================================================

def check(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(message)
    print(f"  PASS: {message}")


def product_lengths(result):
    """Lengths of the products whose status is 'product', smallest first."""
    return sorted(p["length"] for p in result["products"] if p["status"] == "product")


def site_of(result, primer):
    """The first site found for one primer."""
    return [s for s in result["sites"] if s["primer"] == primer][0]


# -- Case 1: exact match, one product ----------------------------------------
# target = 10 filler + 52 bp amplicon + 10 filler
# forward binds "+" at 10..26, reverse binds "-" at 46..62, product 10..62 = 52 bp
def case_exact_match():
    target = filler(10) + amplicon() + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 1: exact match", result)
    check(product_lengths(result) == [52], "exactly one product, 52 bp (16 + 20 + 16)")
    product = result["products"][0]
    check((product["start"], product["end"]) == (10, 62), "product spans 10-62 (printed 11-62)")


# -- Case 2: reverse-strand matches ------------------------------------------
# Reverse-complement the whole Case 1 target. The product is the same 52 bp,
# but now the REVERSE primer is the "+" site and the FORWARD primer is "-".
def case_reverse_strand():
    target = reverse_complement(filler(10) + amplicon() + filler(10))
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 2: whole target on the other strand", result)
    check(product_lengths(result) == [52], "exactly one product, still 52 bp")
    check(result["products"][0]["left"]["primer"] == "reverse", "reverse primer is now the '+' site")
    check(result["products"][0]["right"]["primer"] == "forward", "forward primer is now the '-' site")


# -- Case 3: introduced mismatches at the 3' end -----------------------------
# Forward site: last base (amplicon offset 15) C -> G, distance 1 from 3' end.
# Reverse site: first plus-strand base (amplicon offset 36) C -> T. The reverse
# primer's 3' end is the LEFT end of a "-" site, so this is also distance 1.
# In the reverse primer's own direction: its 3' base G now faces genome A.
# Severity (version 4): the forward primer's C sits opposite template C
# (complement of genome G): C-C is SEVERE. The reverse primer's G sits
# opposite template T (complement of genome A): G-T is MILD.
def case_mismatches():
    seq = mutate(mutate(amplicon(), 15, "G"), 36, "T")
    target = filler(10) + seq + filler(10)

    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 3a: mismatches, tolerance 0", result)
    check(product_lengths(result) == [], "no product when no mismatches are allowed")
    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "mismatched", "forward is 'mismatched'")
    check(result["assay"] == "no product", "assay is 'no product'")
    check(result["near_misses"]["forward"]["changes"] ==
          [{"from_3prime": 1, "primer": "C", "genome": "G", "severity": "severe"}],
          "forward near-miss: 1 from 3' end, primer C, genome G, severe")
    check(result["near_misses"]["reverse"]["changes"] ==
          [{"from_3prime": 1, "primer": "G", "genome": "A", "severity": "mild"}],
          "reverse near-miss: 1 from 3' end, primer G, genome A, mild")

    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 3b: mismatches, tolerance 1", result)
    check(product_lengths(result) == [52], "one product when 1 mismatch is allowed")
    check(result["products"][0]["left"]["mismatch_from_3prime"] == [1],
          "forward mismatch reported at the 3'-terminal base")
    check(result["products"][0]["right"]["mismatch_from_3prime"] == [1],
          "reverse mismatch reported at the 3'-terminal base")
    check(result["products"][0]["left"]["three_prime_risk"] == "high", "forward site: 3' risk HIGH (severe C-C)")
    check(result["products"][0]["right"]["three_prime_risk"] == "low", "reverse site: 3' risk LOW (mild G-T)")
    check(result["products"][0]["three_prime_risk"] == "high", "product takes the worse grade: HIGH")
    check(len(result["warnings"]) == 1, "one 3' risk warning is printed")


# -- Case 3c: mismatch far from the 3' end -----------------------------------
# Change the forward site's FIRST base (offset 0): distance 16 from the 3' end.
def case_mismatch_5prime():
    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 0, "C") + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 3c: mismatch at the 5' end", result)
    check(result["products"][0]["left"]["changes"] ==
          [{"from_3prime": 16, "primer": "G", "genome": "C", "severity": "mild"}],
          "forward mismatch 16 from 3' end: primer G, genome C, mild (G-G)")
    check(result["products"][0]["three_prime_risk"] is None, "a 5' mismatch gives no 3' risk")


# -- Case 4: multiple products -----------------------------------------------
# Two copies of the amplicon: 10 filler + amplicon + 30 filler + amplicon + 10.
# Copy 1 at 10..62, copy 2 at 92..144. Products with max_length=1000:
#   copy1 F x copy1 R = 52 bp, copy2 F x copy2 R = 52 bp,
#   copy1 F x copy2 R = 144 - 10 = 134 bp  (the long "outer" product)
# copy2 F x copy1 R faces away -> no product.
def case_multiple_products():
    target = filler(10) + amplicon() + filler(30) + amplicon() + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 4: two copies of the target", result)
    check(len(result["sites"]) == 4, "4 binding sites (2 forward, 2 reverse)")
    check(product_lengths(result) == [52, 52, 134], "products of 52, 52 and 134 bp")

    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0, max_length=100)
    print_report("Case 4b: same, max product length 100", result)
    check(product_lengths(result) == [52, 52], "the 134 bp product is dropped when the limit is 100")


# -- Case 5: primers facing away from each other -----------------------------
# Put the reverse site FIRST and the forward site after it:
# they point away from each other, so nothing is amplified.
def case_facing_away():
    target = filler(10) + REVERSE_SITE + INSERT + FAKE_FORWARD + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 5: primers facing away", result)
    check(len(result["sites"]) == 2, "both primers still bind")
    check(result["assay"] == "no product", "but no product forms")


# -- Case 6: no binding site at all ------------------------------------------
def case_no_site():
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, filler(200), max_mismatches=2)
    print_report("Case 6: target without the primer sites", result)
    check(len(result["sites"]) == 0, "no sites")
    check(result["assay"] == "no product", "assay is 'no product'")
    check(result["near_misses"]["forward"] is None, "no near-miss either: nothing is close")


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 3: CASES SOLVABLE BY HAND: BAD SEQUENCING DATA (version 2)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each case imitates a trace that poor sequencing leaves in a finished genome
# and checks the model says "not assessable" instead of "mismatched".
# =============================================================================

# -- Case 7: Ns inside a primer site -----------------------------------------
# Replace amplicon offsets 5 and 6 (inside the forward site) with N.
# On the "+" strand, offset 5 is 16-5 = 11 and offset 6 is 16-6 = 10 bases
# from the 3' end. With tolerance 0 the Ns must NOT count as mismatches.
def case_n_in_site():
    seq = mutate(mutate(amplicon(), 5, "N"), 6, "N")
    target = filler(10) + seq + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 7: Ns inside the forward site", result)
    forward_site = site_of(result, "forward")
    check(forward_site["mismatches"] == 0, "Ns are not counted as mismatches")
    check(forward_site["unknown_from_3prime"] == [10, 11], "Ns reported 10 and 11 bases from the 3' end")
    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "not assessable", "forward is 'not assessable'")
    check(result["outcomes"]["reverse"] == "binds", "reverse still binds")
    check(result["assay"] == "not assessable", "assay is 'not assessable'")


# -- Case 7b: same Ns, but 2 mismatches allowed (version 4) ------------------
# 0 real mismatches + 2 unknown bases = 2, which still fits an allowance of 2:
# even if both Ns were mismatches the primer would bind, so the missing data
# cannot change the answer. The site is "binds", not "not assessable".
def case_n_cannot_change_answer():
    seq = mutate(mutate(amplicon(), 5, "N"), 6, "N")
    target = filler(10) + seq + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=2)
    print_report("Case 7b: Ns inside the forward site, tolerance 2", result)
    check(site_of(result, "forward")["outcome"] == "binds", "forward binds: the Ns cannot change the answer")
    check(result["assay"] == "product", "assay is 'product'")


# -- Case 8: sequence ends partway through a primer site ---------------------
# target = 10 filler + forward site + insert + first 12 bases of the reverse
# site. The reverse site would span 46..62 but the sequence stops at 58, so
# 12 of its 16 bases are present (>= 10 required) and all of them match.
def case_truncated_end():
    target = filler(10) + FAKE_FORWARD + INSERT + REVERSE_SITE[:12]
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 8: sequence stops inside the reverse site", result)
    check(site_of(result, "reverse")["reason"] == "runs off the end of the sequence",
          "reason is 'runs off the end'")
    check(result["outcomes"]["reverse"] == "not assessable", "reverse is 'not assessable'")
    check(result["assay"] == "not assessable", "assay is 'not assessable'")


# -- Case 9: sequence starts partway through a primer site -------------------
# Drop the first 4 bases of the amplicon: 12 of the forward site's 16 bases
# remain at the very start of the sequence, so it "runs off the start".
def case_truncated_start():
    target = amplicon()[4:] + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 9: sequence starts inside the forward site", result)
    forward_site = site_of(result, "forward")
    check(forward_site["start"] == -4, "forward site would have started 4 bases before the sequence")
    check(forward_site["reason"] == "runs off the start of the sequence", "reason is 'runs off the start'")
    check(result["assay"] == "not assessable", "assay is 'not assessable'")


# -- Case 10: real mismatches next to missing data ---------------------------
# Three real mismatches in the reverse site (amplicon offsets 40, 44, 48)
# plus an N in the forward site. Tolerance 1: the reverse primer has more
# real differences than allowed, so it is "mismatched". Because the reverse
# primer cannot bind anywhere, no product is possible whatever the N hides:
# the assay is "no product", NOT "not assessable" (fixed in version 3).
# The 3 mismatches are spaced 4 bases apart, cutting the reverse site into
# stretches of at most 4 bases, so the near-miss search (which needs an exact
# 5-base stretch) reports "none close". This shows that limit honestly.
# Version 4: the forward site has 0 mismatches + 1 N, which fits an allowance
# of 1 even if the N is a mismatch, so the forward primer now "binds".
def case_mismatched_beats_unknown():
    seq = amplicon()
    for offset in (40, 44, 48):
        seq = change_base(seq, offset)
    seq = mutate(seq, 3, "N")
    target = filler(10) + seq + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 10: reverse truly mismatched, N elsewhere", result)
    check(result["outcomes"]["reverse"] == "mismatched", "reverse is 'mismatched'")
    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "binds", "forward binds: 1 N fits an allowance of 1")
    check(result["assay"] == "no product", "assay is 'no product': the reverse primer cannot bind")
    check(result["near_misses"]["reverse"] is None,
          "near-miss not found: no exact 5-base stretch left (known limit)")


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 4: CASES SOLVABLE BY HAND: EDGE CASES (version 3)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Situations the earlier cases did not cover.
# =============================================================================

# -- Case 11: a primer pairs with itself -------------------------------------
# Put the forward primer's reverse complement where the reverse site would be.
# The forward primer now binds "+" at 10..26 AND "-" at 46..62, so it makes a
# 52 bp product on its own; the reverse primer binds nowhere.
def case_self_pairing():
    target = filler(10) + FAKE_FORWARD + INSERT + reverse_complement(FAKE_FORWARD) + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 11: forward primer pairs with itself", result)
    product = result["products"][0]
    check((product["left"]["primer"], product["right"]["primer"]) == ("forward", "forward"),
          "the product is forward x forward")
    check(product_lengths(result) == [52], "it is 52 bp")
    check(result["outcomes"]["reverse"] == "mismatched", "the reverse primer does not bind")


# -- Case 12: overlapping primer sites ---------------------------------------
# A second reverse primer whose site starts INSIDE the forward site:
# site = last 5 bases of the forward site + first 11 bases of the insert.
# Forward site 10..26, overlapping reverse site 21..37 -> product 10..37 = 27 bp.
OVERLAP_REVERSE = reverse_complement(FAKE_FORWARD[-5:] + INSERT[:11])


def case_overlapping_sites():
    target = filler(10) + FAKE_FORWARD + INSERT[:11] + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, OVERLAP_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 12: primer sites overlap by 5 bases", result)
    check(site_of(result, "reverse")["start"] == 21, "reverse site starts at 21, inside the forward site")
    check(product_lengths(result) == [27], "one 27 bp product")


# -- Case 13: mismatch allowance too high for the primer length --------------
# 16 bases // (3 + 1) pieces = 4 bases per piece, shorter than k = 5,
# so the search cannot guarantee it finds every site. It must stop with an error.
def case_allowance_too_high():
    print("\n--- Case 13: 3 mismatches allowed on a 16-base primer ---")
    try:
        run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, amplicon(), max_mismatches=3)
        check(False, "an error is raised")
    except ValueError as error:
        print(f"  error message: {error}")
        check(True, "an error is raised instead of a silently incomplete search")


# -- Case 14: palindromic primer binds both strands at the same spot ---------
# GCATGCATATGCATGC is its own reverse complement, so ONE place in the target
# is a "+" site and a "-" site at once (both 10..26). The two sites face each
# other, but the "product" would be only 16 bp (< 20 minimum): no product.
PALINDROME = "GCATGCATATGCATGC"


def case_palindrome():
    target = filler(10) + PALINDROME + filler(10)
    result = run_model(PALINDROME, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 14: palindromic primer", result)
    strands = sorted((s["strand"], s["start"]) for s in result["sites"] if s["primer"] == "forward")
    check(strands == [("+", 10), ("-", 10)], "same spot found on both strands")
    check(result["assay"] == "no product", "no product (16 bp is below the 20 bp minimum)")


# -- Case 15: degenerate base in the primer ----------------------------------
# Forward primer with Y (= C or T) at offset 8: GTTCAGAGYTACTGAC.
# Genome C or T at that spot -> 0 mismatches. Genome A -> 1 mismatch,
# 16 - 8 = 8 bases from the 3' end, reported as "primer Y, genome A".
DEGENERATE_FORWARD = mutate(FAKE_FORWARD, 8, "Y")


def case_degenerate_primer():
    for genome_base in ("C", "T"):
        target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 8, genome_base) + filler(10)
        result = run_model(DEGENERATE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
        print_report(f"Case 15: primer Y, genome {genome_base}", result)
        check(site_of(result, "forward")["mismatches"] == 0, f"Y matches genome {genome_base}")

    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 8, "A") + filler(10)
    result = run_model(DEGENERATE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 15: primer Y, genome A", result)
    check(site_of(result, "forward")["changes"] ==
          [{"from_3prime": 8, "primer": "Y", "genome": "A", "severity": "mild"}],
          "Y does not match genome A: 8 from 3' end, primer Y, genome A, mild")


# -- Case 16: probe binds inside the product ---------------------------------
# Probe = the 20-base insert, which sits between the primer sites.
def case_probe_binds():
    target = filler(10) + amplicon() + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, probe=FAKE_PROBE, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 16: probe binds inside the product", result)
    check(result["products"][0]["probe"] == "binds", "probe binds inside the 52 bp product")
    check(result["assay"] == "product", "assay is 'product'")


# -- Case 17: primers bind but the probe does not ----------------------------
# Three real mismatches in the insert (amplicon offsets 18, 25, 31), tolerance 1.
# Both primers still bind and copy the DNA, but the probe cannot bind, so a
# qPCR machine would see no fluorescence: "no signal".
def case_probe_mismatched():
    seq = amplicon()
    for offset in (18, 25, 31):
        seq = change_base(seq, offset)
    target = filler(10) + seq + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, probe=FAKE_PROBE, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 17: probe has 3 mismatches", result)
    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "binds" and result["outcomes"]["reverse"] == "binds",
          "both primers bind")
    check(result["products"][0]["probe"] == "mismatched", "the probe does not bind")
    check(result["assay"] == "no signal", "assay is 'no signal'")


# -- Case 18: deletion inside a primer site ----------------------------------
# Delete 2 bases from the middle of the forward site (amplicon offsets 6-7).
# Without gaps this looks like many mismatches; the near-miss search should
# explain it as ONE event: a 2-base deletion. (2 is the longest deletion a
# 16-base primer can show: 16 - 2 = 14 = MIN_MATCHED_BASES.)
def case_deletion():
    seq = amplicon()
    target = filler(10) + seq[:6] + seq[8:] + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 18: 2-base deletion in the forward site", result)
    miss = result["near_misses"]["forward"]
    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "mismatched", "forward is 'mismatched'")
    check(miss["events"] == 1, "near-miss is 1 event, not many mismatches")
    check((miss["indel"]["kind"], miss["indel"]["length"]) == ("deletion", 2), "explained as a 2-base deletion")


# -- Case 18b: a 6-base deletion is too long for a 16-base primer -----------
# Delete 6 bases (offsets 5-10): only 10 primer bases would still match,
# fewer than MIN_MATCHED_BASES (14), so the model refuses to guess.
def case_deletion_too_long():
    seq = amplicon()
    target = filler(10) + seq[:5] + seq[11:] + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 18b: 6-base deletion in a 16-base primer site", result)
    check(result["near_misses"]["forward"] is None, "no near-miss: too few matching bases to be sure")


# -- Case 19: insertion inside a primer site ---------------------------------
# Insert TTT into the middle of the reverse site (after amplicon offset 43).
def case_insertion():
    seq = amplicon()
    target = filler(10) + seq[:44] + "TTT" + seq[44:] + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 19: 3-base insertion in the reverse site", result)
    miss = result["near_misses"]["reverse"]
    check(result["outcomes"]["reverse"] == "mismatched", "reverse is 'mismatched'")
    check(miss["events"] == 1, "near-miss is 1 event")
    check((miss["indel"]["kind"], miss["indel"]["length"]) == ("insertion", 3), "explained as a 3-base insertion")


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 5: CASES SOLVABLE BY HAND: VERSION 4 LOGIC FIXES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Genome ambiguity codes, graded 3' risk, and binding through a small
# insertion/deletion in the primer's 5' half. (Case 7b above covers the
# "missing data cannot change the answer" fix.)
# =============================================================================

# -- Case 20: ambiguity codes in the genome ----------------------------------
# The forward primer has C at offset 8 (8 bases from the 3' end).
#   genome Y (C or T): might match, might not      -> unknown
#   genome R (A or G): cannot match a C             -> certain mismatch
#   primer Y vs genome Y: every option is accepted  -> certain match
def case_genome_ambiguity():
    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 8, "Y") + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 20a: primer C, genome Y", result)
    check(site_of(result, "forward")["unknown_from_3prime"] == [8], "genome Y is unknown, not a mismatch")
    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "not assessable", "forward is 'not assessable'")

    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 8, "R") + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 20b: primer C, genome R, tolerance 0", result)
    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "mismatched", "genome R is a certain mismatch: 'mismatched'")
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 20b: primer C, genome R, tolerance 1", result)
    check(site_of(result, "forward")["changes"] ==
          [{"from_3prime": 8, "primer": "C", "genome": "R", "severity": "severe"}],
          "reported as primer C, genome R, severe")

    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 8, "Y") + filler(10)
    result = run_model(DEGENERATE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 20c: primer Y, genome Y", result)
    forward_site = site_of(result, "forward")
    check(forward_site["outcome"] == "binds" and forward_site["unknown_from_3prime"] == [],
          "primer Y fully accepts genome Y: a certain match")


# -- Case 21: graded 3' risk -------------------------------------------------
# a) Only the reverse site's 3'-terminal mismatch (amplicon offset 36 C -> T):
#    G-T is mild, so the product's 3' risk is LOW.
# b) The forward site's 3'-terminal base is N, tolerance 1: the site binds
#    even if the N is a mismatch, but the 3' end is uncertain: POSSIBLE.
def case_graded_risk():
    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 36, "T") + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 21a: one mild mismatch at the 3' end", result)
    check(result["products"][0]["three_prime_risk"] == "low", "product 3' risk is LOW")

    target = filler(10) + mutate(amplicon(), 15, "N") + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 21b: N at the forward primer's 3' end", result)
    check(site_of(result, "forward")["outcome"] == "binds", "forward binds even if the N is a mismatch")
    check(result["products"][0]["three_prime_risk"] == "possible", "product 3' risk is POSSIBLE")


# -- Case 22: 1-base deletion in the primer's 5' half ------------------------
# Delete amplicon offset 2 (a T, 14 bases from the 3' end; the T beside it
# makes 15 an equally good answer). The 3' half is intact, so with 1 mismatch
# allowed the forward primer still binds, counting the gap as 1 mismatch.
# The product loses 1 base: 51 bp. With 0 mismatches allowed it does not bind.
def case_small_deletion_5prime():
    seq = amplicon()
    target = filler(10) + seq[:2] + seq[3:] + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 22: 1-base deletion in the 5' half, tolerance 1", result)
    forward_site = site_of(result, "forward")
    check((forward_site["indel"]["kind"], forward_site["indel"]["length"]) == ("deletion", 1),
          "forward binds through a 1-base deletion")
    check(forward_site["indel"]["from_3prime"][0] > 8, "the deletion is in the 5' half")
    check(product_lengths(result) == [51], "product is 51 bp (one base shorter)")

    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=0)
    print_report("Case 22: same, tolerance 0", result)
    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "mismatched", "with 0 allowed the gap is too much")


# -- Case 22b: 1-base deletion in the primer's 3' half -----------------------
# Delete amplicon offset 13 (a G, 3 bases from the 3' end). A gap that close
# to the 3' end is not allowed to bind; the near-miss search explains it.
def case_small_deletion_3prime():
    seq = amplicon()
    target = filler(10) + seq[:13] + seq[14:] + filler(10)
    result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=1)
    print_report("Case 22b: 1-base deletion in the 3' half", result)
    check(result["outcomes"]["forward"] == "mismatched", "forward is 'mismatched'")
    check(result["near_misses"]["forward"]["indel"] ==
          {"kind": "deletion", "length": 1, "from_3prime": (3, 3)},
          "near-miss: 1-base deletion 3 bases from the 3' end")


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 6: CHECKING THE SEARCH ITSELF
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The k-mer search is fast because it skips most positions. These checks make
# sure it never skips a real site, and never invents near-misses.
# =============================================================================

def brute_force_sites(primer, target, max_mismatches):
    """The slow way: compare the primer at EVERY position on both strands."""
    found = set()
    for strand, pattern in (("+", primer), ("-", reverse_complement(primer))):
        for start in range(-len(pattern) + 1, len(target)):
            mismatches, unknowns = compare_site(target, start, pattern)
            if len(mismatches) <= max_mismatches and len(pattern) - len(unknowns) >= MIN_KNOWN_BASES:
                found.add((strand, start))
    return found


def random_test_target(rng):
    """A 300-base random target with mutated primer copies, Ns/Ys and maybe a cut end."""
    target = [rng.choice("ACGT") for _ in range(300)]
    for _ in range(4):
        copy = list(FAKE_FORWARD if rng.random() < 0.5 else reverse_complement(FAKE_FORWARD))
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
            copy[rng.randrange(len(copy))] = rng.choice("ACGT")
        position = rng.randrange(-6, 300 - len(copy) + 6)
        for i, base in enumerate(copy):
            if 0 <= position + i < len(target):
                target[position + i] = base
    for i in range(len(target)):
        if rng.random() < 0.02:
            target[i] = rng.choice("NY")
    return "".join(target)


# -- Case 23: fast search finds exactly what the slow search finds -----------
# 200 random targets x mismatch allowances 0, 1 and 2. Plain (ungapped) sites
# from the model must equal the slow every-position search exactly.
def case_search_complete():
    print("\n--- Case 23: fast search vs slow every-position search ---")
    rng = random.Random(23)
    compared = 0
    for _ in range(200):
        target = random_test_target(rng)
        for max_mismatches in (0, 1, 2):
            result = run_model(FAKE_FORWARD, FAKE_REVERSE, target, max_mismatches=max_mismatches)
            fast = {(s["strand"], s["start"]) for s in result["sites"]
                    if s["primer"] == "forward" and s["indel"] is None}
            slow = brute_force_sites(FAKE_FORWARD, target, max_mismatches)
            if fast != slow:
                raise AssertionError(f"fast {sorted(fast)} != slow {sorted(slow)} for {target}")
            compared += len(slow)
    check(True, f"600 searches agree with the slow search ({compared} sites compared)")


# -- Case 24: no invented near-misses on a random genome ---------------------
# A random 30,000-base sequence (the size of SARS-CoV-2) should not contain
# the CDC N1 primers or probe, and the near-miss search must not invent a
# "close" site there. (Before the MIN_MATCHED_BASES rule, it did.)
def case_random_genome():
    print("\n--- Case 24: CDC N1 primers on a random 30,000-base sequence ---")
    rng = random.Random(24)
    genome = "".join(rng.choice("ACGT") for _ in range(30000))
    result = run_model("GACCCCAAAATCAGCGAAAT", "TCTGGTTACTGCCAGTTGAATCTG", genome,
                       probe="ACCCCGCATTACGTTTGGTGGACC")
    check(result["sites"] == [], "no binding sites")
    check(all(miss is None for miss in result["near_misses"].values()), "no near-misses invented")


# =============================================================================
# SECTION 7: RUN EVERY CASE
# =============================================================================

if __name__ == "__main__":
    case_exact_match()
    case_reverse_strand()
    case_mismatches()
    case_mismatch_5prime()
    case_multiple_products()
    case_facing_away()
    case_no_site()
    case_n_in_site()
    case_n_cannot_change_answer()
    case_truncated_end()
    case_truncated_start()
    case_mismatched_beats_unknown()
    case_self_pairing()
    case_overlapping_sites()
    case_allowance_too_high()
    case_palindrome()
    case_degenerate_primer()
    case_probe_binds()
    case_probe_mismatched()
    case_deletion()
    case_deletion_too_long()
    case_insertion()
    case_genome_ambiguity()
    case_graded_risk()
    case_small_deletion_5prime()
    case_small_deletion_3prime()
    case_search_complete()
    case_random_genome()
    print("\nAll cases passed.")

1	# =============================================================================
2	# FIRST MODEL: FACTOR: SPECIFICITY   (version 4)
3	# =============================================================================
4	# 02-120 project: Do early SARS-CoV-2 qPCR primers still match later variants?
5	#
6	# This preliminary model answers one question only: given a primer pair (and
7	# optionally a probe) and a target sequence, which PCR products could the
8	# pair amplify, and would the probe detect them?
9	#
10	# What it does:
11	#   - indexes the target's k-mers so primers are not slid across every position
12	#   - finds primer binding sites on BOTH strands
13	#   - allows a user-chosen number of mismatches
14	#   - reports each mismatch by its distance from the primer's 3' end, the
15	#     base change (primer base vs genome base) and how severe that kind of
16	#     mismatch is (severe or mild)
17	#   - grades mismatches close to the 3' end as "3' risk: high / low / possible"
18	#   - accepts degenerate bases in primers (Y = C or T, R = A or G, N = any, ...)
19	#     and reads ambiguity codes in the genome (genome Y = C or T)
20	#   - lets a site with a 1-base insertion/deletion in the primer's 5' half
21	#     still bind (it counts as 1 mismatch)
22	#   - pairs sites that face each other at a plausible distance into products
23	#   - checks that the qPCR probe binds inside each product
24	#   - for every primer that fails, reports its closest near-miss site,
25	#     including a single insertion or deletion
26	#   - gives every primer one of THREE outcomes:
27	#       binds           - a site within the mismatch allowance
28	#       mismatched      - no such site: too many real A/C/G/T differences
29	#       not assessable  - the only candidate site touches missing data
30	#
31	# Positions are stored 0-based inside the code (Python style) and PRINTED
32	# 1-based, the way the CDC table and genome browsers count.
33	#
34	# What it does NOT do yet (left for later models):
35	#   - melting temperature / annealing temperature (nearest-neighbor model)
36	#   - primer dimers
37	#
38	# Files that go with this model (all in journal/):
39	#   test_first_model_factor_specificity.py - fake, hand-solvable test cases
40	#                                            plus search-completeness tests
41	#   cdc_reference_check.py                 - CDC N1/N2/N3 (+ RNase P control)
42	#                                            on the real reference genome
43	#   test_cases_specificity.txt             - every test case and its outcome
44	#   modification documentation.md          - every problem found and fixed
45	#
46	# Run the tests with:     python3 journal/test_first_model_factor_specificity.py
47	# Run the CDC check with: python3 journal/cdc_reference_check.py
48	# =============================================================================
49	#
50	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
51	# HANDLING BAD SEQUENCING DATA
52	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
53	# The genomes this project uses are finished consensus sequences from NCBI:
54	# reads were already aligned and assembled by whoever uploaded them, so read
55	# alignment tools (Salmon, STAR, TopHat) are not needed here. Poor sequencing
56	# still leaves two traces in a finished genome:
57	#
58	#   1. Unknown bases: regions that did not sequence well are written as N, and
59	#      uncertain bases as IUPAC codes (Y, R, ...).
60	#   2. Missing ends: the genome starts or stops partway into the reference.
61	#
62	# Version 1 counted an N as a mismatch, so missing data could look like a
63	# mutation and a primer could be wrongly reported as lost. Since version 2 the
64	# model never counts unknown or missing bases as mismatches. A site whose KNOWN
65	# bases fit the mismatch allowance, but which overlaps N/ambiguous bases or
66	# runs off either end of the sequence, is reported as "not assessable" instead
67	# of "binds" or "mismatched".
68	#
69	# GC content is deliberately NOT used to judge data quality: a FASTA genome has
70	# no quality scores, and SARS-CoV-2 has genuinely AT-rich regions that a GC
71	# filter would wrongly throw away.
72	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
73	
74	
75	# =============================================================================
76	# SECTION 1: DNA HELPERS (complements, degenerate bases, known bases)
77	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
78	# A primer that binds the minus strand appears on the plus strand as its
79	# reverse complement, so we need a way to compute it. Ambiguity codes
80	# (N, Y, R, ...) are complemented too.
81	#
82	# Degenerate primers: some published primers and probes contain IUPAC codes
83	# (the CDC N3 probe has a Y). A primer Y matches a genome C or T.
84	#
85	# Ambiguity codes in the GENOME are read for what they say, not thrown away:
86	#   every base the genome letter could be is accepted by the primer -> match
87	#   none of them is accepted                                        -> mismatch
88	#   some are, some are not                                          -> unknown
89	# e.g. primer C vs genome Y (C or T) is unknown, primer C vs genome R (A or G)
90	# is a certain mismatch, primer Y vs genome Y is a certain match.
91	# Anything that is not a DNA letter at all (e.g. "-") is unknown.
92	# =============================================================================
93	
94	COMPLEMENT = {
95	    "A": "T", "T": "A", "C": "G", "G": "C",
96	    "R": "Y", "Y": "R", "S": "S", "W": "W", "K": "M", "M": "K",
97	    "B": "V", "V": "B", "D": "H", "H": "D", "N": "N",
98	}
99	
100	# which genome bases each primer letter accepts
101	IUPAC = {
102	    "A": "A", "C": "C", "G": "G", "T": "T",
103	    "R": "AG", "Y": "CT", "S": "CG", "W": "AT", "K": "GT", "M": "AC",
104	    "B": "CGT", "D": "AGT", "H": "ACT", "V": "ACG", "N": "ACGT",
105	}
106	
107	KNOWN_BASES = "ACGT"   # anything else in a target counts as unknown data
108	
109	
110	def reverse_complement(seq):
111	    """Return the reverse complement of a DNA string (5'->3')."""
112	    return "".join(COMPLEMENT[base] for base in reversed(seq.upper()))
113	
114	
115	def clean_oligo(name, seq):
116	    """Uppercase a primer/probe and make sure every letter is a DNA/IUPAC code."""
117	    seq = seq.upper()
118	    bad = sorted(set(seq) - set(IUPAC))
119	    if bad:
120	        raise ValueError(f"{name}: not DNA letters: {''.join(bad)}")
121	    return seq
122	
123	
124	def base_matches(genome_base, primer_base):
125	    """True if the genome base is one the primer letter accepts."""
126	    return genome_base in IUPAC[primer_base]
127	
128	
129	def genome_vs_primer(genome_base, primer_base):
130	    """Return 'match', 'mismatch' or 'unknown' for one genome letter facing one primer letter."""
131	    could_be = IUPAC.get(genome_base)
132	    if could_be is None:
133	        return "unknown"   # not a DNA letter at all
134	    accepted = IUPAC[primer_base]
135	    if all(base in accepted for base in could_be):
136	        return "match"
137	    if not any(base in accepted for base in could_be):
138	        return "mismatch"
139	    return "unknown"
140	
141	
142	def expand_degenerate(seq):
143	    """Every plain A/C/G/T sequence a degenerate sequence stands for (YA -> CA, TA)."""
144	    options = [""]
145	    for base in seq:
146	        options = [option + choice for option in options for choice in IUPAC[base]]
147	    return options
148	
149	
150	# =============================================================================
151	# SECTION 2: K-MER INDEX OF THE TARGET SEQUENCE
152	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
153	# Instead of comparing a primer to every position of the target, we record
154	# where every length-k word (k-mer) occurs. Looking up a primer's k-mers then
155	# tells us the only places worth checking. A degenerate k-mer is looked up as
156	# every plain k-mer it stands for.
157	# =============================================================================
158	
159	def build_kmer_index(target, k):
160	    """Map each k-mer in target to the list of positions (0-based) where it starts."""
161	    index = {}
162	    for position in range(len(target) - k + 1):
163	        kmer = target[position:position + k]
164	        index.setdefault(kmer, []).append(position)
165	    return index
166	
167	
168	def seed_hits(index, seed):
169	    """All target positions where a (possibly degenerate) seed occurs exactly."""
170	    hits = []
171	    for plain in expand_degenerate(seed):
172	        hits += index.get(plain, [])
173	    return hits
174	
175	
176	# =============================================================================
177	# SECTION 3: COMPARING A SITE TO THE PRIMER (mismatches vs unknown bases)
178	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
179	# Polymerase extends from the primer's 3' end, so a mismatch there matters
180	# far more than one at the 5' end. Each mismatch is reported as its distance
181	# from the 3' end: 1 = the very last (3'-terminal) base of the primer.
182	#
183	# Positions are split into two kinds:
184	#   mismatch - the genome letter certainly differs from what the primer accepts
185	#   unknown  - the genome has N/an ambiguity code that might or might not
186	#              match, or the position lies beyond the start or end of the
187	#              sequence (no data at all)
188	#
189	# Each mismatch is also described as a base change, both bases written in the
190	# primer's own 5'->3' direction: "primer C, genome G" means the primer has a C
191	# where a perfectly matching primer would need a G.
192	# =============================================================================
193	
194	def compare_site(target, start, pattern):
195	    """Return (mismatch offsets, unknown offsets), left to right on the plus strand."""
196	    mismatches, unknowns = [], []
197	    for offset, primer_base in enumerate(pattern):
198	        position = start + offset
199	        if position < 0 or position >= len(target):
200	            unknowns.append(offset)
201	            continue
202	        verdict = genome_vs_primer(target[position], primer_base)
203	        if verdict == "mismatch":
204	            mismatches.append(offset)
205	        elif verdict == "unknown":
206	            unknowns.append(offset)
207	    return mismatches, unknowns
208	
209	
210	def distances_from_3prime(offsets, length, strand):
211	    """Convert plus-strand offsets into distances from the primer's 3' end.
212	
213	    On the plus strand the primer reads left to right, so its 3' end is the
214	    RIGHT end of the site. On the minus strand the primer reads right to left
215	    along the plus strand, so its 3' end is the LEFT end of the site.
216	    """
217	    if strand == "+":
218	        return sorted(length - offset for offset in offsets)
219	    return sorted(offset + 1 for offset in offsets)
220	
221	
222	def describe_changes(target, pattern, pairs, strand):
223	    """Describe each mismatched (pattern offset, target position) pair as a base change."""
224	    changes = []
225	    for offset, position in pairs:
226	        primer_base, genome_base = pattern[offset], target[position]
227	        if strand == "-":   # turn both back into the primer's own direction
228	            primer_base, genome_base = COMPLEMENT[primer_base], COMPLEMENT[genome_base]
229	        changes.append({
230	            "from_3prime": distances_from_3prime([offset], len(pattern), strand)[0],
231	            "primer": primer_base,
232	            "genome": genome_base,
233	            "severity": mismatch_severity(primer_base, genome_base),
234	        })
235	    return sorted(changes, key=lambda change: change["from_3prime"])
236	
237	
238	# =============================================================================
239	# SECTION 3b: HOW SEVERE IS A MISMATCH? (graded, not all-or-nothing)
240	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
241	# Not every mismatch hurts PCR equally. In a mismatch, the primer base sits
242	# opposite a TEMPLATE base (the complement of the genome base shown in the
243	# report). Measured effects near the 3' end (Stadhouders et al. 2010,
244	# J Mol Diagn 12:109-117; Kwok et al. 1990, Nucleic Acids Res 18:999-1005):
245	#   severe - primer-template A-A, G-A, A-G and C-C: these block extension
246	#            strongly (large rise in Ct, or no product)
247	#   mild   - every other pairing, e.g. G-T, T-G, T-T, T-C: the polymerase
248	#            often extends through them with only a small delay
249	# A degenerate letter counts as severe if ANY base it stands for is severe.
250	#
251	# Severity changes the 3' risk grade below; the mismatch allowance still
252	# counts every mismatch as 1, so the search guarantees in Section 4 hold.
253	# =============================================================================
254	
255	SEVERE_PAIRS = {("A", "A"), ("G", "A"), ("A", "G"), ("C", "C")}   # (primer, template)
256	
257	
258	def mismatch_severity(primer_base, genome_base):
259	    """'severe' or 'mild' for a primer base facing the template opposite genome_base."""
260	    template = COMPLEMENT[genome_base]
261	    for primer_option in IUPAC[primer_base]:
262	        for template_option in IUPAC[template]:
263	            if (primer_option, template_option) in SEVERE_PAIRS:
264	                return "severe"
265	    return "mild"
266	
267	
268	# *****************************************************************************
269	# *****************************************************************************
270	# ***                                                                       ***
271	# ***   >>> USER SETTING: 3' END RISK WINDOW <<<                            ***
272	# ***                                                                       ***
273	# ***   Mismatches this many bases (or fewer) from the 3' end give the      ***
274	# ***   site and its product a 3' risk grade (default: 3):                  ***
275	# ***     high     - a severe mismatch in the window                        ***
276	# ***     low      - only mild mismatches in the window                     ***
277	# ***     possible - no mismatch, but an unknown base in the window         ***
278	# ***   The site still counts as binding; the grade is a warning.           ***
279	# ***                                                                       ***
280	# *****************************************************************************
281	# *****************************************************************************
282	THREE_PRIME_WINDOW = 3
283	RISK_ORDER = [None, "possible", "low", "high"]   # least to most worrying
284	
285	
286	def three_prime_risk(changes, unknown_from_3prime):
287	    """Grade the 3' end of one site: 'high', 'low', 'possible' or None."""
288	    near = [c for c in changes if c["from_3prime"] <= THREE_PRIME_WINDOW]
289	    if any(c["severity"] == "severe" for c in near):
290	        return "high"
291	    if near:
292	        return "low"
293	    if any(d <= THREE_PRIME_WINDOW for d in unknown_from_3prime):
294	        return "possible"
295	    return None
296	
297	
298	def worst_risk(*risks):
299	    """The most worrying of several 3' risk grades."""
300	    return max(risks, key=RISK_ORDER.index)
